prompt:
Use the attached image as the design and pose reference: keep its side-on, left-facing three-quarter owl, its head, body, clock, legs, tail, and its three hanging mechanisms (armillary sphere front, ribbed cylinder hanging in the air below the belly, gear ring at the rear) exactly in place; change only the wings: redraw each wing as the rigid blades described below, in the four wing poses described below. Paint a new picture of the Keeper of Time, a large crownless mechanical owl, mysterious rather than monstrous, hovering and flapping slowly.

The picture is a 2x2 grid of four equal cells with no dividing lines between them, read left to right, top row then bottom row, each cell holding one whole owl. Every owl is in pure side view facing left, level camera, the same scale, filling about 80% of its cell height, with its body centre on the same spot in every cell and wide empty space around it. Body, head, clock, legs, tail and the three hanging mechanisms keep the same size and place in all four; only the wings move. Both wings show: the near wing in front, the far wing just behind and slightly darker.
Cell 1: both wings raised high above the back, tips pointing up.
Cell 2: wings on the downstroke, spread back, tips a little above level.
Cell 3: wings swept low below the body, tips pointing down.
Cell 4: wings on the upstroke, tips trailing a little below level, bent at the elbow.

The owl is a machine, not an animal: nothing on it is feather, fur, skin or flesh. A compact round torso of overlapping riveted bronze plates, centred on an aged clock face with Roman numerals, glass and exactly one long hand on a pivot. A broad, flat, owl-shaped head, wider than tall, made of bolted metal plates with no ear tufts, no crest and no hooked parrot profile: a big flat round facial disc of engraved brass that fills the front of the head, a straight heavy brow plate across it, a short, small, downturned beak of dark metal set low and tight to the disc, one dull, muted round glass eye set in a ring on the disc, and a second small dull glass eye set on the very top of the head between the ear plates. Two very broad wings, each a fan of about eight long flat rigid blades of perforated, ridged sheet metal with straight cut edges and rivets, like a folding fan or a window shutter. Every blade is a straight flat metal strip with a squared-off chisel-cut tip, equal width along its length, laid edge to edge with a visible gap between blades, three visible hinge pins along the wing's spar: no feathers, no barbs, no tapered or pointed feather tips, no scale rows, no curved quills. Each wing joins the torso at a bevelled shoulder spar and hinge. Two short mechanical legs ending in exactly two clawed feet, hanging in the air with no ground. A tail of stacked flat metal plates. Clearly below the body hang exactly three separate mechanisms, spread along the length of the owl: under the beak at the far left hangs a small armillary sphere; under the middle of the belly, directly below the clock, hangs a ribbed cylinder with solid bronze walls; under the tail at the far right hangs a toothed gear ring. Each has one small dull eye on its underside. Each mechanism hangs on its own single straight, thin chain of small links that runs in a clean line up to the small glass eye on top of the head: three separate chains fanning out from that one point, never crossing each other, never tangled, no knots, no loops, no extra chain anywhere. The mechanisms are far apart, hang below the legs' height, and none touches the wings, neck or feet.

Style: a dark etched storybook engraving for a 2D game sprite. Brown-black ink line #171614 with a heavy dark outer contour, sepia wash, fine cross-hatching and visible paper tooth on the owl only. Metal in mid-tone warm bronze and pewter steel, lit surfaces a warm tan bronze #B08D5E and pale steel #A89C8C, shaded surfaces #5C473E, with warm ivory highlights #EFE0C0, so most of the owl reads as mid-tone and light metal, with a matte hand-engraved finish, dense hatching and no glossy gradients or airbrushed shine; only the ink lines and the deepest recesses are near black. Just inside the contour runs a thin rim light in warm candle-cream #FFF3D6 (leaning red-orange, never lemon or lime). Only the clock face glows, a soft gold #E9C46A. Every colour on the owl is a warm brown, gold or cream.

Background: the whole picture, every pixel outside the owls and between the four cells, is one single flat pure green #00FF00, identical in the top row and the bottom row, with no gradient, vignette, glow, haze, white, texture, text or shadow anywhere. The owls have no soft glow and no blur around their contours: crisp hard edges against the green, and no green anywhere on the owls.
